title: Shelach: go and see (Numbers 13:1–2)
hook: twelve scouts are sent to see the land

segments.voice: Yesterday, five words for Miriam, and your line, short prayers count. Did someone hurting get a name and a few words from you? Today a new portion, and the people are at the edge of the land. Day four hundred forty-six.

Before you sign a lease, you visit the apartment. You open the closets, run the shower, check whether the windows face a brick wall. Before a big move, people drive through the new town at night to see if it's quiet. Nobody wants to commit to a place sight unseen. The Israelites are camped in the wilderness of Paran, at the edge of the promised land. The next step is to walk in. And first, someone wants a look around. Today's portion begins with two words, and a story that takes the rest of this week to tell.
screen: `VISIT BEFORE YOU SIGN.` → `AT THE EDGE OF THE LAND.` → `FIRST, A LOOK AROUND.`

segments.voice: God says to Moses: "Send thou men, that they may spy out the land of Canaan". In Hebrew, shelach lecha: send for yourself. That extra word, lecha, for yourself, caught Rashi's eye. He reads it as permission, not command: send, if you want to; I'm not ordering it. Why would God put it that way? Because, in Deuteronomy, Moses remembers that the people asked for it. They wanted a report first. So twelve men go, one leader from each tribe. One of them, Hoshea, gets a new name from Moses: Yehoshua, Joshua. Then Moses gives them a list of questions, and it's a careful list. See the land, what it is. The people living there: strong or weak, few or many. The cities: open camps or fortified. The soil: rich or poor. Are there trees? And be of good courage, he says, and bring back some of its fruit. It was the season of the first ripe grapes. They go for forty days, from the south to the far north. Past Hebron, in a valley later called Eshcol, cluster, they cut a single bunch of grapes so heavy that two men carry it between them on a pole. Pomegranates and figs too. Looking isn't the problem. Moses asked them to see, and to bring back something real. The verb for their mission, latur, means to scout, to explore, to go around and look. Seeing for yourself is a good instinct. What you do with what you saw, as we'll find, is the test.
screen: `SHELACH LECHA: SEND FOR YOURSELF.` · `TWELVE SCOUTS, ONE PER TRIBE.` · `MOSES' LIST: SEE WHAT IT IS.` · `A CLUSTER CARRIED BY TWO.` · then, large: `GO AND SEE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: go and look for yourself. Breathe, and think of one thing you've formed an opinion about secondhand: a neighborhood, a coworker, a restaurant, a group of people, a book you've only heard about. Notice where the opinion came from. A review? A rumor? Then picture going to see: walking down that street, having that coffee, reading that first chapter. Then ask Moses' first question: what is it, really? The bell holds the time.
Shelach. Send: the portion where twelve scouts go to see the land, and bring back a cluster of grapes too big for one man.
Your line: go and see. Today, check one secondhand opinion with your own eyes, and bring back something real. Day four hundred forty-six.

howItsDone: Shelach is read in synagogue in the yearly Torah cycle; the image of two scouts carrying a giant grape cluster on a pole is a familiar one in Jewish art, and the story of the scouts is studied as a lesson in how people see and report.

fork.setup: you're Moses, sending scouts into the land. what do you ask them to bring back?
options: nothing; just a yes or no.
answers about the land and its people, and some of its fruit.
fork.reveal: Moses asks them to see what it is, strong or weak, rich or poor, and to be of good courage and bring back fruit.

original.note: Hebrew: send for yourself. the portion's opening words.

trapdoor: what you thought: God ordered the spy mission.
what it means: the words are send for yourself, and Rashi hears permission, given because the people asked.
what a scholar hears: Rashi on Numbers 13:2 reads lecha, for yourself, alongside Deuteronomy 1:22, where the people request the scouts.

notes: Numbers 13:2 fragment quoted from JPS 1917 from memory; confirm.
'Two years out of Egypt': the departure from Sinai is in the second year (Numbers 10:11); the scouts are sent soon after. Confirm phrasing.
Latur (t-w-r) glossed as to scout, explore; confirm.
